solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place vacated, with luck, before a game

indicators.note: a place vacated has its inside emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or luck

explanation.surface: Someone empties a place, hoping for luck, before a match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties the word 'Place', keeping only its first and last letters; 'before' simply orders the pieces. PELOTA is a Basque ball game played against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a fast court game of Basque origin, played with a ball and a curved basket or the hand.

clue.text: Weapon used to dump the girlfriend?

definitions.meaning: a military device that projects burning fuel
a flame is an old sweetheart, and one who throws over a flame dumps her

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: an old flame is a former girlfriend, and to throw someone over is to dump them.
explanation.definitionFit: This weapon shoots a stream of burning fuel; the cryptic half reads it as a person who casts off a sweetheart.

clue.text: Blessed with a lot of money — about a ton!

indicators.note: the large sum goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a fortune is a very large sum

explanation.surface: Someone lucky enough to be rich, with roughly a hundred pounds extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and T inside FORTUNE, splitting it as FORTUN-AT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blessed in this sense is to be lucky, favoured by good fortune.

clue.text: Liaison with a French blonde?

parts.note: fair hair is blonde hair

explanation.surface: A romance with a fair-haired Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship, a synonym for a love affair.

clue.text: What's the point!

parts.note: read not as a weary question but as a description of the punctuation point that ends this very clue

explanation.definitionFit: The clue ends with this punctuation mark, which is literally a point, the one standing at the end of an exclamation.

clue.text: Ran to protect fool, being worried

indicators.note: a protector stands round what it guards, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: hared means ran fast
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to shield an idiot, feeling anxious all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' signals a container: the fool is shielded inside the word for ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed means pestered and troubled, synonymous with worried or stressed.

clue.text: Fat on beef stew regularly vanishing

indicators.note: every other letter disappears at a steady interval, leaving alternate letters

explanation.surface: A dieter watches the fat on a beef stew being skimmed off bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly vanishing' drops every second letter of ON BEEF STEW, keeping the first, third, fifth and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone very overweight, a medical synonym for fat.

clue.text: Admission of charm

definitions.meaning: the right or act of going in somewhere
as a verb, to bewitch or delight, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently: EN-trance (a way in) and en-TRANCE (to enchant).
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is an entry or way in; to charm someone is to put them in a spell, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Long-legged bird with no tail makes champion

indicators.note: the bird's name loses its final letter, its tail end

parts.note: the heron is a tall wading bird with long legs

explanation.surface: A wading bird without its tail feathers wins the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is someone celebrated for winning or for brave deeds, a synonym for a hero.

clue.text: Ship's doctor tried initially, cutting heart

indicators.note: one group of letters slices into another, sitting inside it

parts.note: the core is the heart of something
a vet is an animal doctor

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A ship's medic attempts first to operate on someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T from 'tried'; VET and T together go 'cutting' into CORE: COR-VETT-E. The 's of 'Ship's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast warship used for escort duties.

clue.text: Pay for degree students' game

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: Funding someone's degree course so the students can play their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner (as on British L-plates), so LL is a pair of students.
explanation.definitionFit: Football is a team ball game, the example of game meant here.

clue.text: Views a wife as rock

parts.note: sees means views or looks at
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogy tables

explanation.surface: A man regards his wife as his steady support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is the verb here, not a noun: to swing back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to move to and fro, which is what seesaw means as a verb.

clue.text: Principal sets up computers

parts.note: main means chief or principal
frames means sets up someone falsely to look guilty

explanation.surface: The head teacher installs the school's new computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets up' means framing someone for a crime, not installing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainframes are large, powerful central computers used by organisations.

clue.text: Wife once ate like a bird, noisily, to be pregnant

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: the word is to be judged by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a bird pecked at its food

explanation.surface: A former wife who barely ate is, it turns out, carrying a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' signals that PECT stands for the spoken word 'pecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be expecting is the idiom for carrying a baby, so expect stands for being pregnant.

clue.text: The wheels of justice?

parts.note: the phrase for the slow machinery of the courts is read literally as a vehicle driven by the police

explanation.definitionFit: A police vehicle on its beat is literally a set of wheels serving law enforcement.

clue.text: Queen serving up hock to a revolutionary Iran

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: hock is a cut of ham from a pig's leg

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A queen is offered a joint of meat by a rebellious Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' turns HAM into MAH; 'revolutionary' rearranges IRAN into RANI.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is an Indian queen or the wife of a maharajah.

clue.text: Quoted from note pinched by detectives

indicators.note: the detectives hold the note between them, enclosing it

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A line quoted from a letter seized by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police; 'pinched by' means held inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cited is to be quoted or referred to as evidence or authority.

clue.text: Start business trading right for name

indicators.note: the letter for right is swapped out and the letter for name put in its place

parts.note: commerce is the activity of trading and business

explanation.surface: A firm begins trading, exchanging the right one for a famous brand.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in COMMERCE is replaced by N (name), giving COMMENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence is a formal synonym for begin or start.

clue.text: Recovered from putting time into short film role

indicators.note: one piece goes within another, inserted between its letters

parts.note: a cameo is a brief appearance by a known actor in a film

explanation.surface: An actor bounced back after fitting a bit-part into the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... into' places T inside CAMEO: CAME-T-O. The answer is a phrase: to come to means to regain consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round after fainting is to regain consciousness, which is what recovered means here.

clue.text: How a satellite's transport could be affected?

definitions.text: How a satellite's transport could be affected?

parts.words: How a satellite's transport could be affected?
parts.note: the satellite is the Moon and its transport a lorry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means dazed or lovesick, here punningly split into a lorry belonging to the Moon.

clue.text: Arts programme on Italian channel

indicators.note: to programme is to arrange or order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An arts show broadcast on an Italian television station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' rearranges 'Arts'; 'channel' is a sea passage, not a TV station.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea channel joining two larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Where gamblers find answer in tossing coins

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the rearranged group
tossing scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Gamblers look for the answer in the toss of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' rearranges COINS to CSINO, and 'in' puts A inside it: C-A-SINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling house, the place where those who bet are found.

clue.text: A word of greeting, and leaves mostly in the morning

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a salad is a dish of green leaves
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A greeting offered while picking salad leaves early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final letter of the leafy dish; 'leaves' is a noun, not the verb of departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaam is an Arabic greeting meaning peace, used as a salutation.

clue.text: Farewell that's sort of cast in gold?

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a mould or stamp used to cast or shape metal

explanation.surface: A goodbye gift cast in solid gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' points to the metal-shaping mould, not throwing dice or actors; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French-derived word for goodbye, a synonym for farewell.

clue.text: A principled lecturer failed in hearing about exam

indicators.note: the sounded word goes around the exam, enclosing it
the word is judged by how it sounds to a listener, not its spelling

parts.note: missed means failed to hit
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An upright professor flunked an oral examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' turns 'missed' into a sound-alike spelling; 'about' wraps that round the spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist is someone who lectures others on right and wrong, a principled preacher.

clue.text: Criminal had a nice spread

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook laid on a lovely meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is a ranch or estate (a large spread of land), not a buffet of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch in Spanish-speaking countries; a spread is slang for a ranch.

clue.text: Relative finding pleasure trip started late

indicators.note: the word begins late, its first letter missing

parts.note: a jaunt is a short trip for pleasure

explanation.surface: A family member turns up after a holiday got going behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: JAUNT loses its J under 'started late'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relative.

clue.text: Reckons Catherine runs from such a cool performer

parts.note: figures means reckons or works out
Kate is a short form of the name Catherine
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Catherine reckons she will escape from someone icy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' points to the ice on which this performer works; R for runs comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater performs routines on ice, so a cool performer in the chilly sense.
